doc.headline: Quality costs money in a steady ladder: Brisk-S is cheapest at {cost_per_1k.brisk-s|usd} per 1k conversations, Atlas-L best on overall quality at {cost_per_1k.atlas-l|usd}; the owner must price a point.
doc.lede: Nothing was declared, so no option is ruled out and none dominates. Open-70B is never the best buy: Brisk-S and Atlas-M beat it at every price per point.

caveats.material_if: only if the owner has a quality floor or exchange rate that rules an option out; none was declared.
only if a reader needs a paired gap between two arms; the arms are compared on their own figures and intervals.
only if the judge favours one arm's style; cost is measured telemetry and does not rest on it, but the quality ladder does.
only if one arm leads by little; the ladder's steps are wide against the half-widths, so a re-run is unlikely to reorder it.

decision.text: Moving from Brisk-S to Atlas-M buys {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.gain|pts} overall quality for {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.cost_gap|usd} more per 1k conversations; moving on to Atlas-L buys {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain|pts} more for {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.cost_gap|usd} more.

Brisk-S is the best buy below about {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point|usd} per quality point, Atlas-M up to about {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point|usd}, Atlas-L above that. Open-70B is never best.

Our lean, not a rule: Atlas-M as the middle step, because Brisk-S is weakest on troubleshooting and Atlas-L's extra points are the most expensive. It holds only for prices per point between the two steps.
The owner declaring a price per quality point and a floor on the weakest task, troubleshooting; and a paired run for intervals on the gaps.

doc.headline: Atlas-L scores highest on overall quality and Brisk-S costs least; each step up costs sharply more per point, so the owner must price a point, at this run's unknown provider routing.
doc.lede: Pooled overall quality runs from {pooled.overall.brisk-s.mean} for Brisk-S through {pooled.overall.atlas-m.mean} for Atlas-M to {pooled.overall.atlas-l.mean} for Atlas-L, at {cost_per_1k.brisk-s|usd}, {cost_per_1k.atlas-m|usd} and {cost_per_1k.atlas-l|usd} per 1k conversations. Nothing was declared, so no option is ruled out and none dominates.

caveats.material_if: only if the owner has a quality floor or exchange rate that rules an option out; none was declared, so the trade stays the owner's.
only if a reader needs a paired gap between two arms; every gap here is unpaired and wider than a paired one would be.
only if the judge favours one arm's style. The quality ordering and the flip prices rest on this judge; the cost figures are measured and do not.
only if an arm leads by little; the steps between arms are wide against the half-widths, so a re-run is unlikely to reorder them, but Atlas-M versus Open-70B on persona small talk is close.

decision.text: Moving from Brisk-S to Atlas-M buys {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.gain} overall quality points for {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.cost_gap|usd} more per 1k conversations; moving on to Atlas-L buys {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain} more for {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.cost_gap|usd} more. Costs depend on unnamed provider routing.

Brisk-S is the best buy below about {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point|usd} per quality point, Atlas-M up to about {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point|usd}, Atlas-L above that; the unpaired bands are {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_low_unpaired|usd} to {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_high_unpaired|usd} and {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_low_unpaired|usd} to {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_high_unpaired|usd}, inside which this run does not settle the call. Open-70B is never best.

Our lean, not a rule: Atlas-M as the middle step, if a point is worth between the two prices. Its own weak side is troubleshooting at {task.trouble.atlas-m.overall.mean} against {task.trouble.atlas-l.overall.mean} for Atlas-L. Brisk-S resolves only {task.trouble.brisk-s.resolves.mean} of troubleshooting cases, and Open-70B confirms before account changes only {task.trouble.open-70b.confirms.mean} of the time.
The owner declaring a price per quality point and floors on troubleshooting resolution and on confirming before account changes; and the provider and pricing basis behind each arm's cost.
